title: Tests that isolate the database
summary: Create test data once, assert the JSON contract, count queries, and cover a missing row with Django's TestCase.

scenario.briefing: The inventory tests depend on rows that happen to exist in the development database, and they never notice the N+1 query. Build a self-contained TestCase with its own data and assertions.

sections.title: The test database is disposable
sections.body: The Django test runner creates a separate database, applies migrations, and removes it afterward. TestCase wraps each test in a transaction and rolls it back, so one test cannot see another test's writes. The development database is never the test target.

sections.title: Share setup, not state
sections.body: setUpTestData runs once per class inside a class-level transaction. It is the right place for rows that every test reads. setUp runs before each test and is the place for per-test state, such as a logged-in client.

sections.title: Query counts are assertions
sections.body: A response can look correct while the view issues one query per row. assertNumQueries(1) around the client call makes the query shape visible and fails when a lazy relation starts querying.

from django.test import TestCase
from django.urls import reverse

from .models import Category, Item


class ItemViewTests(TestCase):
    def test_list_returns_items(self):
        # TODO: create data once and assert the JSON contract
        response = self.client.get(reverse("item-list"))
        self.assertEqual(response.status_code, 200)

steps.title: How Django isolates tests
hints: Think about which database the test runner uses.
TestCase uses a transaction per test.
setUpTestData runs once for the class.
The test client still runs middleware and URL resolution.

statements.label: The test runner creates a separate database instead of using the development one.
TestCase rolls each test back in a transaction.
setUpTestData runs once per test class.
client.get executes the view without middleware or URL resolution.
Data written by one test is visible to the next test in the same class.

steps.explanation: Django builds a separate test database, TestCase rolls each test back, and setUpTestData shares read-only setup rows once per class. The test client still resolves URLs and runs middleware, and test writes do not leak into the next test.
